If the graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above, then

${\int }_{-6}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
We divide the interval of integration into $3$ regions: the arc of the semi-circle for $x\in [-6,-2],$ the line segment for $x\in [-2,2),$ and the line segment for $x\in (2,6].$ Using the additive property of integrals, we write

$$
{\int }_{-6}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-6}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{2}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{3}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-6,-2].$ The corresponding region is an upper semi-circle of radius $2$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\pi (2)^{2} \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-2,2).$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}4\cdot 4 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-8.
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (2,6].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4+1)\cdot 4 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{2}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{3}=-10.
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-6}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2}-{A}_{3} \\  & =2\pi -8-10 \\  & =2\pi -18.\end{aligned}
$$
